deepdive.sec: Specialty Fats & Cocoa Butter Equivalents (CBE) / Edible Oil Value Chain

bull_bear.body: Prioritizing high-ROCE capex (>6x asset turn expected on forward projects); Working capital cycle improved to 125 days (from 151); ROCE 33.6%, ROE 40.3%; No dividend change discussed, focus on reinvestment.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Geopolitical tension (West Africa, West Asia) impacting freight/energy; FX volatility (60% hedged, 40% open); Subsidiary ramp-up delays; Raw material price fluctuation (Shea, Sal, Mango).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly confident, execution-focused, emphasizing long-term vision over quarterly noise; transparent on subsidiary losses as transitional; aggressive on capacity utilization and margin sustainability.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Annual cash profit (PAT+Dep) of INR 259 Cr now exceeds gross block (INR 250 Cr), signaling extreme capital efficiency; Burkina Faso project is government-backed (MoU signed) mitigating political risk; Immediate seed processing in Africa improves fat yield vs. 60-day transport lag.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Completed an INR 500 Cr QIP in July 2026 at ₹1,470/share to strengthen the balance sheet ahead of the FY28 capex cycle.
- Consolidated Net Debt to Equity improved to 0.38 in FY26 from 0.83 in FY25, indicating deleveraging even as growth capex ramped.
- CARE Ratings upgraded the Company's bank facilities from 'A' to 'A+'.
- Reinvestment-led allocation philosophy: proposed INR 460 Cr capex over the next 2-3 years directed at capacity expansion, forward/backward integration and global scale-up rather than the deck disclosing any dividend policy.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: CBE contributed ~30% of revenue (up from 10% two years ago); Stearin + CBE constitute 70%-75% of value-added mix; Solvent Fractionation Plant 2 debottlenecked to 32.5k TPA (+30%), Plant 1 (15k TPA) to follow; Total input capacity heading to 52k TPA.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rising input costs and supply chain inefficiencies in traditional edible oil processors | Manorama Industries Ltd | beneficiary | High | Backward integration in Africa directly addresses 45%-60% of RM cost while improving yield; high-value CBE mix (30% of sales) provides pricing power and margin resilience against commodity cycles. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Niche, high-return specialty fats platform with a ~2-decade track record, built on an end-to-end integrated model from exotic tree-borne seed sourcing (India, Africa) through to global CBE/specialty-fats leadership ("Forest to Formulation").
- Long-standing relationships with Fortune 500 food & confectionery majors (Ferrero, Mondelez, Mars, Hershey, Nestle, Barry Callebaut, Cargill, AAK, Fuji Oil, among others) and personal-care brands (The Body Shop, L'Oreal Paris, Lush), supported by customized product development.
- Geographic reach spans 39+ countries across Asia, Europe, Americas, MENA, Africa and Oceania via 10 international subsidiaries; Export:Domestic revenue mix stood at 60:40 in Q1FY27.
- Government of India Recognized Star Export House with MSME ZED GOLD certification, alongside international certifications (ISO 9001/14001/45001, RSPO, Kosher, Halal/MUI, FSSC 22000, EcoVadis, Sedex SMETA) enabling access to premium global markets.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Awards] Multiple export-excellence recognitions cited in the deck, including the IOPEPC Award for Highest Excellence in Exports of Shea Oil (2024-25), GLOBOIL INDIA 2025 Award for highest exports of Made-in-India CBE, SHEFEXIL Export Excellence Award for 7 consecutive years, and FIEO's 'Highest Foreign Exchange Earner' awards.
- [Leadership] Board led by Ashish Saraf (Chairman & Managing Director) and Vinita Saraf (Vice Chairperson & Whole Time Director), with CA Ashok Jain as Whole Time Director & CFO; R&D led by Dr. Krishnadath Bhaggan (Deputy CEO – Business Development & VP R&D) at a DSIR-certified, Government of India-accredited research center.
- [Shareholding] As of June 2026, Promoter holding was 54.32%, FIIs 3.22%, MF 2.63% and Other 39.83%; Market Cap was INR 10,270 Cr and CMP ₹1,626 (as on 12 Aug 2026).
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Gross margin pressure in consolidated entities (43% vs 48% prior) due to subsidiary startup costs/freight; Standalone margins stable at ~48%; Expect normalization as subsidiaries scale; Logistic cost savings from Africa integration to offset freight inflation.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: >25% (FY27); Margin: Sustain 25%-27% EBITDA; Order Inflow: Strong visibility from global F&B/Cosmetic demand; Capex: INR 460 Cr over 2-3 years (commissioning by FY28).
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Demand-led model with 85%-90% utilization target on expanded 52k TPA capacity; no formal order book disclosed but visibility high via long-term customer partnerships.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Burkina Faso plant (INR 120 Cr) for seed-to-butter conversion (45%-60% RM cost savings, yield improvement); New 75k TPA Solvent Fractionation Plant 3 + CBE facility + 200 TPD refinery (INR 330-340 Cr) for forward integration; Targeting INR 3,500 Cr revenue by FY30.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Manorama Industries delivered exceptional FY26 with 76% revenue growth and 27% EBITDA margins driven by volume surge and high-value CBE mix (now 30% of sales), while initiating a INR 460 Cr capex cycle for African backward integration and forward capacity expansion to sustain >25% growth trajectory through FY28.

meta.thesis: Manorama Industries delivered exceptional FY26 with 76% revenue growth and 27% EBITDA margins driven by volume surge and high-value CBE mix (now 30% of sales), while initiating a INR 460 Cr capex cycle for African backward integration and forward capacity expansion to sustain >25% growth trajectory through FY28.
